# Data Card - Manas Twin synthetic cohort

**Everything in `data/` is synthetic.** It was generated by `src/simulator.py` (seed 42). No real person is represented and no real health data is included.

## Why synthetic
No public dataset combines daily wearable data with longitudinal health records (PHQ-9, diagnoses, medication) for Indian students and young professionals. Simulation lets us build and test the full twin pipeline end-to-end, with known ground truth for evaluation.

## Cohort
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| People | 600 (≈50% students 18–24, 50% professionals 23–35) |
| Follow-up | 240 days each (1 Jan – 28 Aug 2025), 144,000 person-days |
| Cities | 12 Indian cities (Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Delhi NCR, Chennai, Kolkata, ...) |
| Depressive episodes | 175, in 148 people (24.7%) |
| Missing (non-wear) days | 6.5% |
| PHQ-9 screenings / diagnoses | 3,340 / 139 |

The cohort is deliberately **enriched** for episodes (about a quarter of people have one) so the model has enough positive examples. This is far higher than population prevalence.

## Generative model (ground truth, hidden from the twin)
- Each person has a latent depressive load *L(t)*, a mean-reverting process driven by personal vulnerability, prior episodes, family history, comorbidities, **calendar stressors** (exam seasons for students; quarter-end and appraisal cycles for professionals) and random life events.
- An **episode** starts when *L* crosses a threshold and lasts **at least 14 days** (mirroring the two-week criterion for a major depressive episode). Episodes are partly self-sustaining; antidepressant treatment lowers *L* after about 2 weeks.
- **Signals** move away from each person's own baseline in proportion to *L*: shorter sleep (75% of people) or longer sleep (25%), later bedtime, lower sleep efficiency, higher resting HR, lower HRV, fewer steps, more late-night screen time, fewer social contacts. Each person also has an individual "reactivity". Weekends and stress periods add confounding variation, plus day-to-day noise.
- **Help-seeking is slow:** diagnosis happens, if at all, a week or more into an episode. PHQ-9 screenings occur roughly monthly with 70% attendance.

These directions follow the digital-phenotyping literature on depression. The magnitudes are modelling assumptions and are the main reason real-data validation is the next step.

## Files
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `patients.csv` | One row per person: demographics, history, comorbidities. Columns prefixed `gt_` are simulator ground truth, **never used by the model** |
| `daily_wearables.csv.gz` | One row per person-day: the 8 signals, stressor flag, and ground-truth columns (`gt_latent_load`, `gt_in_episode`, `gt_episode_id`, `gt_onset`) used **only** to create labels and evaluate |
| `encounters.csv` | EHR events: PHQ-9 screenings, diagnoses (ICD-10 F32), medication start (ATC N06AB10), therapy referrals. `episode_resolved_gt` rows are evaluation-only |
| `risk_scores.csv.gz` | Twin-model risk for every person-day (dashboard cache) |
| `fhir_samples/` | Example FHIR R4-style bundles |
| `showcase.json` | Demo patients from the held-out test set |
| `cohort_summary.json` | Summary statistics |

## Real-data validation hook
`src/depresjon_loader.py` adapts the public **DEPRESJON** dataset (wrist actigraphy from 23 people with depression and 32 controls; Garcia-Ceja et al., 2018) into daily twin-style activity features. The dataset is not redistributed here. Download it from its source and check its licence before use.
